column4: Visit note | 2025-11-18 03:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Lamia Faruque, 76, female. Mrs. Faruque attends for a follow-up review regarding high cholesterol on a routine test, noting that her father had a heart attack at 55, while she herself remains free of any chest pain or palpitations. She works as a farmer and her elevated reading was originally found in an office health check in Khilgaon. She denies shortness of breath, dizziness, or swelling in her ankles. On examination: LDL cholesterol 4.4 mmol/L, BP 120/72 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 54 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no murmurs, and lung fields are clear. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.
